chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal said: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abdillah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the crescents (of the months). He said: 'They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break your fast.' I said: 'Do you consider if the month is twenty-nine days, do I make up that day?' He said: 'No, unless there is a just testimony to that effect. If they testify that they saw the crescent before that, then make up that day.'

key_terms.أَقْضِي: Make up (performing a missed obligatory act, here referring to fasting a day)
key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةِ: Crescents (plural of hilal, referring to the new moon sighting)
key_terms.الْهِلاَلَ: The crescent (specifically the new moon marking the start of a month)
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ عُدُولٌ: Just testimony (witnesses who are reliable and upright in their testimony)

ai.seo_question: How to determine if a fasting month has 29 or 30 days according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the lunar month is either twenty-nine or thirty days, establishing the principle that a month cannot be twenty-eight days. He specifies that if a month is twenty-nine days, the following day is not automatically considered part of the month; rather, it must be made up (qada) only upon receiving just testimony (shahadat al-'udul) that the crescent was sighted on the previous evening, thereby linking the calendar to empirical evidence rather than fixed calculation alone.
